fact: The Cybersecurity Hub, South Africa's National CSIRT, was established in 2015 by the then Department of Telecommunications and Postal Services, mandated by the National Cybersecurity Policy Framework passed by Cabinet in March 2012, and receives and routes incident reports on weekdays.
The SADC statement of 13 September 2018 says South Africa has an established and operational national CIRT.
ITWeb quotes advocate Jacqueline Fick saying South Africa lacks a national cyber security strategy.
The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies' Deputy Director described the National Cybersecurity Hub as a Computer Security Incident Response Team hosted by the department.
The DCDT reply says that under the 2015 National Cybersecurity Policy Framework it established and in 2016 operationalised a national CSIRT, the Cybersecurity Hub.
Analyst Elmarie Biermann says South Africa has the Cybersecurity Hub as its National Computer Security Response Team, which she rates as dysfunctional.
